cards.name: Pikachu
cards.notes: Pikachu from Lost Origin Trainer Gallery TG05/TG30 is included in this guide as a sleepy Pokemon card for collectors building a calm, cozy, or nap-themed binder. As a Trainer Gallery Rare Holo, it connects nicely with the characterful, scene-driven side of modern Pokemon card collecting. The card is illustrated by Atsushi Furusawa, which is useful context for collectors who like arranging pages by artist as well as by Pokemon. Its higher market price makes it feel like a centerpiece candidate rather than a casual binder filler. It works nicely in a Sword & Shield-era page, especially alongside Trainer Gallery and alternate-art sleepy cards.
cards.whyItBelongs: Adventure can wait. Akari has curled up beneath a tree for a well-earned nap with Pikachu tucked into her arms, and somehow Pikachu has managed to wriggle half-free without waking either of them. Atsushi Furusawa turns a quiet break in Hisui into an incredibly sweet little snapshot of how comfortable these two are together.

cards.name: Pikachu
cards.notes: Pikachu from ME: 30th Celebration 027/128 is included because this little guy is fully asleep and looks like he is dreaming. A very cozy addition to the Pikachu rare group. Suggested by GitHub issue #40.
cards.whyItBelongs: Cozy nap handcrafted in yarn. Asako Ito’s crocheted Pikachu passed out on a felt hill is pure comforting nostalgia.

cards.name: Pikachu
cards.notes: Pikachu from ME: 30th Celebration 043/128 is included because this dreamy beach scene feels like the perfect hammock-side companion to Oshawott from White Flare. Suggested by GitHub issue #41.
cards.whyItBelongs: Cozy nap after soaking in tropical vibes. OOYAMA’s delightfully goofy, round Pikachu has flopped onto its back in the warm sand, cheeks flushed and eyes shut, while a little sailboat drifts by. Look closely by the palm tree: a Weedle is peeking out at the sleeper. Even its attack, Tropical Vibes, puts it to sleep.

cards.name: Eevee
cards.notes: Eevee from Scarlet & Violet Promos 173/150 is included in this guide as a sleepy Pokemon card for collectors building a calm, cozy, or nap-themed binder. As a promo card, it brings a slightly different collecting path than main-set sleepy Pokemon cards. The card is illustrated by Makura Tami, which is useful context for collectors who like arranging pages by artist as well as by Pokemon. It is more of a focused wishlist card than an impulse pickup, especially for collectors building a curated sleepy Pokemon page. It fits especially well in a modern Scarlet & Violet-era binder page built around soft, restful, or cozy card art.
cards.whyItBelongs: Cozy nap curled on a sunny cushion. Eevee rolled into a soft cinnamon loaf next to tea is promo perfection for any cozy binder page.

cards.name: Whimsicott
cards.notes: Whimsicott from Fates Collide 71/124 is included in this guide as a sleepy Pokemon card for collectors building a calm, cozy, or nap-themed binder. As an uncommon card, it is useful for collectors who want the sleepy theme to feel complete beyond only the expensive hits. The card is illustrated by sui, which is useful context for collectors who like arranging pages by artist as well as by Pokemon. Its low market price makes it one of the easiest sleepy Pokemon cards to add to a binder without stretching a collection budget. It gives a binder page a slightly older modern feel, which helps the sleepy Pokemon theme avoid looking too concentrated in recent sets.
cards.whyItBelongs: Cozy nap on a plush floor pillow. Whimsicott sinking into soft bedding is pure cloud-soft comfort that softens any page.
